text:
olivia: FYI customer reported a nasty streaming regression after a network blip — Python SDK v0.12.1, heartbeat enabled. Resume works but final fragment is duplicated, then the async iterator stalls. Customer worried about double billing and lost responses.

kevin: can you paste a minimal repro and the customer SDK config? which region/host?

olivia: quick repro I used locally (python):
```py
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(api_key=...)
it = client.stream(model='rw1', heartbeat_interval=10)
for chunk in it:
    print(chunk)
```
Behavior: after simulating a brief TCP drop, client reconnects, we see the same final chunk printed twice (identical token sequence) and then the iterator hangs (no StopAsyncIteration).

sam: customer logs (sanitized):
```
[2024-03-15T14:02:10Z] connection lost: ECONNRESET
[2024-03-15T14:02:11Z] reconnected, resume ok, seq=12983
> SSE frame: data: {"token":"Hello","seq":12983}
> SSE frame: :heartbeat

> SSE frame: data: {"token":"World","seq":12984}
> SSE frame: data: {"token":"World","seq":12984}
[2024-03-15T14:02:12Z] iterator hang awaiting next frame
```
looks like a heartbeat or injected keepalive got into the stream machinery and resume merged buffers so token 12984 was delivered twice. :eyes:

raj: this matches a bug we patched on another branch — heartbeats were being emitted as comment frames (`:heartbeat`) but our parser sometimes treats comment lines as delimiters and can shift the internal offset calculation for `last_seq`. If the resume ACK logic replays a cached buffer without updating the seq, client sees duplicate data. Need wire trace and SDK parser state.

olivia: uploaded a wiretrace: https://redwood.internal/trace/abc123 (customer consented). Repro steps: 1) start streaming with heartbeat_interval=10, 2) kill connection for ~300ms, 3) proxy returns SSE resume frames with `:heartbeat` inserted between fragments. I can repro with `tc qdisc netem loss 0.2% delay 100ms` or `mitmproxy --repeat-requests`.

lina: suggested quick mitigation in SDK: treat lines that start with `:` or `event: heartbeat` as control-only and never advance the consumer-facing token buffer. Example pseudo-fix in parser:
```
if line.startswith(':') or event == 'heartbeat':
    update_internal_heartbeat_ts()
    continue  # don't append to chunk buffer or increment seq index
```
This avoids exposing heartbeat frames to iterators and keeps seq accounting consistent.

dev-bot: canary: rolled redwood-py 0.12.2-rc1 to staging with heartbeat-parser-fix branch. CI tests added for resume + comment-frame ordering.

kevin: important: if duplicates are emitted upstream they may be counted in billing. @support-bot can we confirm whether duplicated token deliveries on resume are billed and whether we should credit affected customers?

support-bot: billing FYI — duplicates can trigger double token counts in usage logs if the server emits repeated data frames. Flagging invoice review for any customers who reported this incident between 2024-03-15T14:00 and 2024-03-15T14:30.

raj: created INFR-7893 (P2) assigned to eng-runtime + sdk-py. Action items: (1) add strict comment/heartbeat parsing tests, (2) add wiretrace-based integration test that injects `:heartbeat` between fragments, (3) add metrics to detect duplicate seq delivery during resume.

olivia: adding customer contact + thread to the ticket, will request a quick credit if billing shows duplication. Thanks — pls update here when canary results are green.

kevin: noted, will monitor staging canary and escalate to prod rollback if duplicates observed. :thumbsup:
